summary: All twelve findings confirmed; most fixes corrected. Ordering (checked by reachability with the 25 accepted restructurings, link maps, decompositions and promoted blueprints; every proposed link acyclic alone and together): /1 as proposed, plus the same back edge in Bhatt–Mathew-23 route 7; /2 drop PR.3 as a planner of item 084 instead of adding DD.4 → PR.3; /3 the PR.4 half of item 088 must go through PR.1–PR.3, not Theorem 8.17; /4 keep the AI.0/AI.4 → RT.6 links, reject the AI.7 alternative; /5 DD.0 → RT.1 is already pending (RT-AREA-ktheory-2/37), E5:animation → RT.1 is redundant; /6 L.5 → RT.6 right, but item 024 needs Serre's finiteness of the stable stems, not Bökstedt (the paper says so on p. 216). /7: sixteen of the seventeen paper mistakes confirmed; item (7) follows the paper's cohomological convention. /8: 041 and 035 are false, not just loose. /9: nine more wrong locators. /10 confirmed. /11: the Nikolaus–Scholze inputs are owned by that paper's accepted routes (L.5 needs the /6 link); BMS 2018 and Scholze–Weinstein are already prerequisites; w-localization is genuinely missing. /12 confirmed: published p. 285 prints the E8 slip.

Confirmed for sixteen of the seventeen; (7) is not a mistake and should be dropped. I checked each one at its TeX line in arXiv v2 and in the published text. The published pages are 209, 233, 236–237, 239, 222, 246, 247, 258, 262, 261, 268, 270, 273–274, 290, 300, 291 and 301, and I rendered pp. 262, 268, 270 and 300 as images. Every one is printed the same way in both versions. None of them coincides with E1–E12. (9) is two lines before E6 and (10) is in the same sentence as E5, but both are different slips. The errata register holds no other entry for this paper. The mathematics, item by item. (1) Take n = 1 and k algebraically closed. Then Z_p(1)(O_K) = (O_K^×)^∧[−1]: Pic and Br vanish, and T_pμ(K) = 0 because K is discretely valued. By Kummer theory, τ^{≤1}RΓ_ét(K, Z_p(1)) = (K^×)^∧[−1]. The split valuation sequence 0 → (O_K^×)^∧ → (K^×)^∧ → Z_p → 0 gives fibre Z_p[−2], not Z_p(0)(k) = Z_p. So the first term must be WΩ^{n−1}_{log}[−n−1], which is Sato's triangle T1. The Hesselholt–Madsen graded pieces also lack [2n], as the paper's own convention gr^nTC = Z_p(n)[2n] requires. (2) I computed Ext^1_{Ch(R)}(M, N[−1]) directly. An extension is exactly a differential M → N, so the group is Hom_R(M, N) = Ext^{1+c} with c = −1, not Ext^{1−c} = Ext^2. This agrees with the proof's RHom_R(M, N)[c]. In Theorem 5.4, Map_DF(L_iX, Y) = Map(X, Y(i)) gives Ext^a(M[−i], N[−j]) = Ext^{a+i−j}. So both printed exponents have the wrong sign, and after correcting both the argument goes through. (3) For F ∈ Fun(Z^op, D(R)) the maps run F(i) → F(i−1), so 'F(i)/F(i−1)' does not typecheck. Theorem 5.4(3) itself writes gr^i = F(i)/F(i+1). (4) Proposition 5.8 identifies Lη_I K with the underlying object F(−∞), and the next paragraph proves that F ↦ F(−∞) is symmetric monoidal. (5) The groups H^{−i} with i < 0 vanish trivially. The needed statement, and the '= H^{−i}(A/pA) = 0' that follows, is for i > 0. (6) Put u′ = cu and ξ′ = cξ, keeping σ and v. Then can(u′) = ξ′σ and φ(u′) = φ(c)ασ, so c = φ^{−1}(α)^{−1}. A direct check shows that no rescaling of the triple u, v, σ realises ξ′ = φ^{−1}(α)ξ in general. (8) By Proposition 7.8, the graded pieces of 𝒩^i are Ω^j[−j] for j ≤ min(i, d). The printed D^{[0,max(i,d)]} is true but too weak for the 'in particular', since that needs gr^i ∈ D^{≤i}. (9) The relation X_u − u^p adjoins nothing. (10) Z_p(n) is defined in Theorem 1.12(5) (p. 207), not in (4). (11) φ = p^nF in degree n, so degree i+1 carries p^{i+1}FWΩ^{i+1}. (12) I recomputed the cohomology. The kernel of pd on VWΩ^j/p is pWΩ^j, by d^{−1}(pWΩ) = FWΩ, so H^j = pWΩ^j/(pVWΩ^j + pdVWΩ^{j−1}), with index j and with W in dVW. (13) By fibre sequence (4), Lτ^{≤i}Ω is the graded piece 𝒩^i, and 𝒩^{≥i} → Lτ^{≤i}Ω has kernel 𝒩^{≥i+1}, so it is not injective. Theorem 8.14(2) states the correct version. (14) q must be [ε]. The operator γ_i: T_i ↦ qT_i must be an automorphism, and the Frobenius factor is [p]_q = φ(μ)/μ = ξ̃ with q − 1 = μ. (15) B^cy Z is the free loop space, and the unstable Frobenius precomposes a loop with the p-fold cover. So st^n becomes st^{pn}, i.e. (s, n) ↦ (s, pn). Now take τ = t^p acting on the C_p-fixed points by (s, pm) ↦ (τ^m s, pm). The map (s, n) ↦ (s, pn) is equivariant, while (s^p, pn) sends (τ^n s, n) to (τ^{pn}s^p, pn) ≠ (τ^n s^p, pn). (16) Tensoring over a ring k would give Hochschild homology relative to k, not THH, so the correct formula is A ⊗_{E_∞} T^∧_p. The red team's 'no ring k is in scope' slightly overstates: the proof of Proposition 9.10 just before uses k for the residue field of O_C. That does not rescue the formula. (17) Base change of THH needs pushouts, and 𝕊[z] is not a pullback of O_K and 𝕊 over k. The right-hand square is a pushout for flat A or for the derived tensor product. Why (7) is not a mistake: the sentence is internally consistent in cohomological indexing, which the paper uses for bare 'bounded above/below'. In the proof of Theorem 5.4 it writes 'bounded above complexes K^• (i.e. K^i = 0 for i ≫ 0)', and where homological indexing is meant it says 'homologically bounded below' explicitly (§2). In that indexing the Postnikov limit τ_{≤n}M is cohomologically bounded below. The phrase 'so after shifting coconnective' says exactly that, and 'bounded above as well', via colim τ_{≥−n}, is also right. Read homologically, the text would contradict itself in the same clause ('bounded below, so … coconnective'), so the red team's swap is a change of convention, not a correction. Right fix: add sixteen sourceIssues, E13–E28 (the seventeen without (7)), kind misprint, known 'new', with searched as proposed. Give each locator with its published page and arXiv v2 page. (2) is one entry naming both slips, Proposition 5.6 and the proof of Theorem 5.4, noted as self-cancelling. (1) names both missing shifts. For (8), I would set affects to 'nothing' rather than 'the proof'. The printed bound is true, the intended min makes the 'in particular' follow, and the section 18 definition of 'nothing' ('the mathematics is right as intended') applies. The reason should say that max is too weak for the consequence. All the others affect nothing.

Confirmed. I checked each item against the TeX and the published text. 040 copies Proposition 5.6's Ext^{i−c}. It should be Ext^{i+c}, as shown under finding 7(2). 059 copies D^{[0,max(i,d)]}. It should be min(i, d). 106 copies (s, n) ↦ (s^p, pn). It should be (s, n) ↦ (s, pn), as shown under finding 7(15). 041's 'exactly when' is not just stronger than Remark 5.9's 'if': it is false. Over R = Z_p with I = (p), take the triangle Z/p[−1] → 0 → Z/p. Lη_p kills both Z/p[−1] and Z/p, because it divides each H^i by its p-torsion. So Lη_p gives 0 → 0 → 0, which is an exact triangle. Yet the boundary H^i(Z/p ⊗^L Z/p) → H^{i+1}(Z/p[−1] ⊗^L Z/p) is an isomorphism, hence nonzero. In Beilinson terms, the defect is the image of the boundary map as a chain complex, and that image can be acyclic. The item should say 'if'. 035's unqualified 'equivalently S = R/I' is also false, not just less precise. Take R = ∏_n O_C, which is perfectoid, and f = (p^n)_n, a nonzerodivisor. Then L_{S/R} = S[1] has p-complete Tor amplitude in degree −1. But S = ∏_n O_C/p^n is p-complete with unbounded p^∞-torsion, so it is not quasisyntomic and not quasiregular semiperfectoid. The paper's sentence after Lemma 4.25 includes the condition 'p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion', which the item must restore. 005 mispairs its 'resp.' chains. Definition 4.10 (pp. 223–224) pairs quasismooth with L_{B/A} p-completely flat and a (quasisyntomic) cover with p-completely faithfully flat plus Tor amplitude in [−1, 0]. 111: Remark 11.14 says the filtration is compatible with the Nygaard filtration via Corollary 11.12(1) and (3), and with the Hodge filtration via the de Rham comparison. The item should say this. The remark cites that comparison as 'Theorem 11.2(2)'; the fixer can word it as 'the de Rham comparison (2)'. 070 states Lemma 7.22 faithfully. Adding the extension to all quasisyntomic O_C-algebras, which the proof of Proposition 7.21 asserts on p. 264, is a sensible completeness fix, but it is not a correction. The note additions to 066 and 064 are right, since the slips are real (finding 7(9) and 7(10)). 001: R07.4 plans 'Frobenius modules and the height bound determined by the Eisenstein polynomial'. AI.7 warns that torsion cohomology modules are not finite-free Kisin modules but defines no torsion-allowed notion. Neither pins down Definition 1.1: a finitely generated 𝔖-module, torsion allowed, with M ⊗_{φ} 𝔖[1/E] ≅ M[1/E]. That is the notion Theorem 1.2 needs. I would direct the requests entry to R07.4, whose title is 'Breuil–Kisin modules' and which AI.7 already requires, rather than AI.7. Either stage works. Minor point: the finding's 'where' field omits 106 and 111, which its claim and fix cover.

Confirmed. I read the files at Mathlib 082e2d3. (a) Right. Mathlib.RingTheory.Perfectoid.FontaineTheta declares WittVector.fontaineTheta (line 165). Outside the WittVector namespace it declares surjective_fontaineTheta (line 195), whose hypotheses are [Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R)], [IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R] and hF : Function.Surjective (frobenius (ModP R p) p). No declaration fontaineTheta_surjective exists at the pin; the declaration index has none. That name occurs only in the file's own module docstring, which is probably where the extraction took it from. The counterexample is right. For R = Z_p⟨T⟩ we have R/p = F_p[T]. An element with p^n-th roots for every n lies in the intersection of the F_p[T^{p^n}], which is F_p, so the inverse-limit perfection is F_p.
